thread:
aya: FYI nightly perf run showed a p99 spike on the long-context workload after the kernel-selector change landed last night. p50 stable, p99 up ~2.3x on 40k-token traces :thinking:

mike: ugh. any diffs in throughput or CPU/GPU utilization?

aya: throughput (tokens/s) steady for bulk, but tail latency distribution is heavier. attached minimal logs below.

aya: ```
# nightly-summary: model=xl-attn, seq=40960, batch=1
baseline (old-selector): p50=87ms p95=210ms p99=360ms
new-selector (rollout=100%): p50=92ms p95=240ms p99=830ms
# no obvious GPU mem spikes, utilization ~84% both runs
```

sam: have we checked correctness? tail could be retries or blocking due to fallback. are outputs identical?

aya: good call. I ran a small correctness sweep vs gold (float32 fused-attn-v1). result: most prompts match, but ~0.6% tokens show logit deltas > 1e-2 and we saw 3 examples with NaN in the quantized path.

lisa: NaNs are concerning. which kernel is producing them? fused-attn-v2 with int8 quant path?

aya: yep: kernel-selector prefers fused-attn-v2 (optimized for long seq) and uses the quant pathway for devices flagged as "quant-ready". NaNs only show up when both conditions true.

indra: could be a race in the KV scratch buffer or a bad transpose in the fused path. did you capture stacktrace or backtrace when NaN occurs?

aya: grabbing a stackframe is tricky in prod but I reproduced locally. snippet: ```
E 2026-02-12 03:12:34.452 kernel.cpp:402 compute_attention: softmax produced NaN for head=7 seq=40960
E backtrace: fused_attn_v2::compute -> softmax_kernel -> expf -> NaN
```

mike: hmm expf NaN suggests an Inf or bad memory read. any OOB access? ASAN run?

aya: ASAN build on the fused kernel spot-check failed to reproduce OOB, but valgrind-ish memcheck showed a misaligned load in an AVX kernel variant. That lines up with performance optimizer reordering loads to 32-byte instead of 64-byte boundaries for that tensor layout.

sam: alignment bug would explain only long-seq hitting it if strides change. still doesn't explain p99 (two different problems?)

lisa: tail could be caused by slow-path fallback when a kernel hits NaN and we re-run on safe kernel; re-run would add big latency for that request. check logs for fallback events.

aya: yes. logs contain fallback events like: ```
W fallback: kernel=v2 produced NaN, retrying with fused-v1 (safe)
# retry added ~470ms on top of run time for that request
```

indra: that matches: p50 unaffected, but a small fraction with retries cause big p99 increase. Root cause is the NaN-producing fused-attn-v2 path.

mike: immediate mitigation: roll back selector to prefer fused-attn-v1 for seq>8192 (or disable quant path) until we fix. can we push a canary first?

aya: I already triggered a partial rollback in staging and started a canary job (canary=5% traffic) — dev-bot should post status.

dev-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rollout started for selector-rollback @ 5% to region-us-west-2. CI job: ci/nightly/attn-canary-178045. Monitoring p99 in realtime.

sam: longer term: add deterministic cross-kernel diff test to CI that runs a representative set of long/short prompts and checks: (a) no NaNs, (b) max logit delta < 1e-3, (c) perplexity delta < 1e-4. If diff > threshold, fail.

lisa: agree. also add metric to tracing: kernel-fallback.count and fallback.latency to correlate with tail spikes.

mike: action items: 1) mike - coordinate rollback & canary (ETA 30m). 2) sam - add regression test + MSE threshold to ci/attn-smoke. 3) aya - collect failing prompts and attach to ticket. 4) indra - audit fused-attn-v2 memory access patterns for alignment and quant conversion code (assign if ok).

aya: I'll upload a tarball with 120 failing prompts and their gold logits to the ticket: TKT-1247. sample repro command: ```
# reproduce locally (cpu/gpu build)
./bazel-bin/eng/runtime/bench_attn --model xl-attn --seq 40960 --kernel fused-attn-v2 --prompt-file failing_prompts.jsonl --dump-logits=out.log
```

indra: I'll start with a microbench stressing contiguous vs strided head layouts and run with -fsanitize=undefined on x86. expect to push a patch for aligned loads if I find it.

sam: for the CI diff test, propose we run 50 prompts with seeds pinned and compare logits using L2 norm. if any sample L2 > 1e-3 -> fail. Also include a NaN check. I can draft a pytest and infra hook.

mike: sounds good. once canary is stable for 2 hours we'll promote rollback and schedule deeper root-cause triage.

lisa: thank you for quick triage. please @channel in the ticket when the canary metrics look good or if rollback is required. :thumbsup:

aya: noted, uploading artifacts now. thanks team :eyes:
